Subject: Upcoming campaign — temporary higher burst & SLA ask

Hi Soojin,

We"re ramping toward a national patient outreach campaign the week of Aug 9 and expect a short spike in inference volume (estimated peak 3–4x our baseline for ~72 hours). Our compliance team is asking whether Redwood can do a short-term carveout to the standard rate-window and burst quotas so we maintain our latency SLO (p95 < 350ms) during the campaign.

Can you confirm:
- Whether a temporary carveout is possible for that window (Aug 9–11) without an Enterprise Dedicated contract
- What guarantees we can get for p95 latency vs current fairness throttling behavior
- Any additional costs or manual steps required

I attached a small traffic forecast (Traffic_Report_Q3.csv). Happy to jump on a short call if easier.

Thanks,
Elena Martinez
Head of Digital Experience
Phoenix Health

Subject: Re: Upcoming campaign — temporary higher burst & SLA ask

Hi Elena — thanks for the heads up and the forecast. Short answer: yes, we can help with a temporary carveout but there are a few tradeoffs depending on whether you want hard latency guarantees or a prioritized burst window.

High level options we typically offer for short windows:
- Priority Burst Window (recommended): reserve a transient priority queue for Aug 9–11, throttle other background tenants minimally. Best-effort p95 target of <350ms; backed by monitoring and an ops escalation path. Requires a nominal one-time fee and a short technical onboarding (routing rule + API key tag).
- SLA-backed Temporary Commitment: commit to a tighter p95 SLA for the window and provision extra capacity; requires short-term commitment and signoff from finance/legal (MPA addendum). Higher cost but formalized SLA and credits if we miss targets.

Can you confirm expected peak rps and whether you can accept a priority-burst approach versus a formal SLA addendum? I"ll loop in Karthik for pricing and Marissa for operational runbook + playbook.

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi Elena — looping in pricing/ops. Quick answers and a proposed commercial path: 

1) Technical feasibility
We can provision a prioritized burst window tied to an API key tag and route your traffic through a higher-priority queue for the defined three-day window. That will significantly reduce the chance of fairness throttling during the spike. For your forecast (~3.5x baseline) we expect p95 in the 220–380ms range depending on sequence lengths; the conservative estimate is 350ms.

2) Commercials
Option A — Priority Burst (operational carveout): one-time setup fee $6,500 + usage at standard rates. No SLA credits.
Option B — Short-term SLA Addendum: $12,500 + committed min throughput and SLA credits (5% credit for p95 > 350ms). Requires countersignature on a short MPA addendum (I attached a proposed draft).

3) Operational requirements
- We need your final traffic window and the list of API keys to tag by Aug 2.
- Runbook: Marissa will prepare a call sheet and escalation path including on-call contacts for Redwood infra.

Please let us know which option you prefer and whether you want us to proceed with the addendum.

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Hi Karthik / Soojin — thanks for the thorough options. We"d prefer Option A (Priority Burst) for speed, but will accept a very small contingency credit if latency degrades beyond your 350ms conservative estimate. Can you confirm the final one-time fee and the tagging steps? Our IT team will provide keys by Aug 1.

A couple of clarifications for the runbook:
- Will the priority queue prevent cross-tenant fairness cuts during the window, or can severe cluster contention still cause temporary throttling?
- If we see sustained degradation, what is the escalation SLA for Redwood to provision extra capacity (time-to-remedy)?

If you can send a short runbook and the final order (invoice) we"ll route for approval.

Best,
Elena
